$comment: Frozen relevance corpus — audit improvement #1. Ages are hours before T0 (2026-01-01T00:00:00Z), resolved by seedRelevanceCorpus against a FakeClock, so the level spread is reproduced rather than asserted per trace. Distractors are deliberate: several traces share 'timeout', 'lock', 'cache' and 'token' in unrelated senses, because a corpus with no near-misses measures nothing. Do not tune this file to make a threshold pass — move the threshold and say why.

memories.content: The auth middleware rejected valid tokens: the expiry check used < instead of <=, so a token expiring on the exact second read as already expired.
Two concurrent requests both refreshed the session token and the second write clobbered the first, logging the user out. Serialising refresh per session fixed it.
Comparing API tokens with === leaks length and prefix through timing. The comparison must be constant-time over a fixed-length digest.
Never put the API token in a query string: it lands in proxy logs and browser history. It belongs in a header.
CORS origin checks must compare whole origins parsed with new URL(), never substrings: evil-example.com passes a substring test against example.com.
Logout left the rendered page in the browser back-forward cache, so the previous user's dashboard reappeared on the back button. Cache-Control: no-store on the document fixed it.
SQLite in WAL mode with busy_timeout at 5000ms removes the SQLITE_BUSY errors seen on concurrent intra-process writes.
The cross-process write lock is a separate SQLite database held in a transaction: the OS releases it when the process dies, including on SIGKILL, so a crash cannot strand the lock.
An in-process search index goes stale when another connection commits. PRAGMA data_version changes on every external commit, which is the cheapest way to know the index must be rebuilt.
A migration that catches every error from ALTER TABLE and calls it 'column already exists' will swallow a disk-full or permission error too. Match the duplicate-column message and rethrow the rest.
Naming the temporary file after the destination plus the PID is not unique: two writes for the same target in one process share it. Use a random suffix per write.
Copying the .db file while writes are in flight is not a backup: the WAL holds committed pages the copy misses. Use the online backup API or a checkpoint under a lock.
Tests that open the production database corrupt real data. The store refuses to open its resolved production path when NODE_ENV is test.
The forgetting curve is driven by levelThresholds in hours: 24 for L1, 168 for L2, 720 for L3, 2160 for L4.
Recall, salience and verification each slow decay, and their product is capped: without the cap a verified, salient, often-recalled trace never fades, which is not forgetting.
A recurring cue rearmed itself but the intention stayed fired, and resolution only considers armed intentions — so the second occurrence never woke anything.
Reading only the first 500 armed cues starves the tail: if the first 500 never match, the rest are invisible on every pass. Page with a cursor instead.
Clamping the relevance score to 100 flattened every bonus: an old trace with no recalls ranked exactly like a fresh, heavily recalled one.
Cron expressions are matched in UTC. A user writing 0 9 * * * in Paris gets a wake at 10:00 or 11:00 local depending on the season.
A user-supplied pattern with nested quantifiers can hang the resolver for minutes. Reject nested quantifiers and fall back to a literal search.
Passing no hostname to serve() binds every interface. The API binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses to start on a non-loopback host without a token.
A 500 that echoes the internal error hands the caller stack frames and paths. Log the detail under a correlation id and return only that id.
Every numeric query parameter goes through a bounded integer parser. A bare parseInt accepts NaN and unbounded values straight into a query.
Content that is not human-verified renders inside an untrusted fence after sanitising. The boundary is per content type, so a new type needs its own wrapping and its own test.
A tooltip built with innerHTML from trace content executed the content. Tooltips and labels are built with createElement and textContent instead.
The dashboard hung forever on a slow upstream because fetch has no default timeout. An AbortController with a deadline turns it into a visible error.

queries.$why: Exact vocabulary of one incident, in a directory full of other token traces.
A security lesson recalled by its mechanism, not its incident.
Two genuinely relevant traces, both about concurrent SQLite access.
The recall that matters most in practice: 'why did my search miss it'.
Degraded trace (aged past L2) still reachable by its keywords.
Distinguishes two cron traces that share vocabulary but not subject.
The mirror of the previous query — same trap in reverse.
Aged well past L2; the incident is remembered by its symptom.
Operational recall with an exact identifier in the content.
Procedural rule, recalled by concept rather than by incident.
'timeout' appears in three unrelated senses. Both busy_timeout and the fetch deadline are defensible answers; the auth traces are not.
Same query, narrowed to one mental place: the store's lock, not the auth race.
A misspelling. This and the two below are what a phonetic encoder is FOR — without them, comparing encoders would only measure the half that favours the strict one.
A misspelling on the discriminating term rather than an incidental one.
Morphological variant: the trace says 'concurrency', the user types 'concurrent'.

A one-word misspelling. The near-miss fallback cannot help here — it needs at least two terms — so this measures the phonetic encoder alone. It is the reason `latin:advanced` is kept despite the precision it costs on q-sqlite-concurrency; swapping to latin:default scores zero here.
Same property on a rarer word, so the result is not an artefact of 'sqlite' being everywhere.
Nothing in the corpus is about this. Returning something confidently is the failure mode being measured.

intentions.content: Review the advisory lock takeover path before the next release.
Re-audit the CORS origin comparison after the router upgrade.
Document the untrusted fence boundary per content type.
Decide whether the model cache belongs in the user profile.

dueCases.$why: Before any cue time: waking anything here is a false positive.
Past the first cue only. The later ones must stay asleep.
Two cues elapsed, the third is still in the future.
loop-cors-audit expires at +48h, well before its cue fires: an expired loop must not wake.

contextCases.$why: Opening in /src/store: the store's open loop belongs in the block, the core one does not.
A loop with no cue at all still belongs in its own directory's block.
A directory with no loops must produce no loops — not the nearest ones.
